messages:
janet_l: During private-deploy network hardening sprints we noticed an intermittent conntrack exhaustion in edge nodes when rate-limiting egress + service mesh mTLS is enabled. Symptoms: established connections drop causing KMS handshakes to fail and leading to quota-fallback behavior. tagging @mike_r @alex_c.
sec-bot: alert: node-priv-edge-04 conntrack_high_watermark=0.87 threshold=0.8
mike_r: conntrack issues show when we apply netpol that blocks cross-namespace pod-to-pod flows. The mesh sidecar is still opening many NATed connections to KMS endpoints. Need to measure ephemeral port usage.
alex_c: mitigation: reduce NAT ephemeral port churn by enabling connection reuse in go-kms-client (keepalive + http2 where possible) and tune sysctl `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` on edge nodes. Also add netpol rule to allow intra-namespace traffic to the `keystore` pods to avoid excessive SNAT.
janet_l: are we comfortable adding intra-namespace allow in netpol? for private deploys we try to keep minimal rule sets.
priya_m: minimal exception just for namespace `priv-keystore` and label `app=keystore` with comment and expiry. we can automate removal via helm hook after upgrade window.
mike_r: also add small monitoring: prom rule for `node_conntrack_count / node_conntrack_max > 0.75` and alert to oncall. add runbook steps: 1) cordon node, 2) increase conntrack, 3) restart kube-proxy.
alex_c: will draft netpol patch and sysctl docs. Also note this impacts private deployments with high TLS handshake rate (attestation flows).
sec-bot: note added to priv-deploy-hardening checklist: conntrack review for high-churn workloads.
janet_l: long-term: evaluate sidecar config that shares listener (proxy-less TLS termination) for keystore pods to reduce NAT. file RFC?
priya_m: created RFC stub `rfc/keystore-conntrack-optim` in docs repo. I'll link shortly.
mike_r: closing for now, will monitor canary. tagging @oncall-ops for watch for next 24h. :eyes:
